logo_override.alt_text: Auckland University of Technology (AUT) - Te Wananga Aronui / Otamaki Makaurau
logo_override.validation_detail: webfetch returned 'Image fetched successfully', confirming HTTP 200 plus a real image content type rather than a WAF interstitial. Decoded and rendered for inspection: the full official AUT lockup - black 'AUT' wordmark with the triangular Aronui mark, over the red Te Wananga Aronui / Otamaki Makaurau bar. Format is jpg, so there is no alpha channel at all and no white-on-transparent variant is possible; the wordmark is black on white and the only colour is AUT red, so it is fully legible on a light card.

notes: AUT does not put the logo in an tag, which is why a naive markup scan finds nothing: the header brand is the bare anchor AUT and the actual mark is a CSS background. Traced it through the site's own stylesheet https://www.aut.ac.nz/_design/design2025/css-2025/global.css?v=0.1.106, whose rule '#topNav #headerLogo' declares background-image: url(https://www.aut.ac.nz/__data/assets/image/0005/1046534/aut-logo.jpg), with '#topNav.shrink #headerLogo' sizing it 90x98. That asset is served from the awarding university's own __data/assets path on aut.ac.nz, so rule 1 holds, and it is AUT's own corporate lockup for a university-awarded doctoral scholarship, so rule 2 holds. Preferred over the favicon https://www.aut.ac.nz/__data/assets/file/0018/747/favicon.ico declared in the same page's , because the brief asks for a full-colour wordmark or crest in preference to a bare icon. Rule 3 was checked by decoding the image rather than trusting the extension: the filename has no 'white' or 'transbg' hint, and the render confirms black-on-white plus red, with no transparency because it is a jpg. Noted but not used: og:image on the page is present but empty (content="").
